objective: Suppliers send overlapping catalogue files; they must be merged into one. Add a module `stockroom/merge.py` with frozen dataclasses `Conflict(sku, before, after)` and `MergeResult(items, conflicts)` (both tuples), and the functions `name_key(name) -> str`, `read_renames(text) -> dict[str, str]` and `merge_catalogues(catalogues, *, prefer='last', renames=None) -> MergeResult`. `name_key` is how names are compared: the name in Unicode NFKC form, split at whitespace runs (`str.split()`) and joined with single spaces, then `str.casefold()` (so `BLUE` U+00A0 `mug`, full-width letters, and `Straße` / `STRASSE` compare equal). Suppliers also renumber SKUs: `renames` is `None` or a mapping `{old_sku: new_sku}` (`None` and `{}` mean no renames). An item's final SKU is found by following the mapping from its SKU until a SKU that is not a key (`MUG-001` -> `MUG-0001` -> `MUG-1001` gives `MUG-1001`; a SKU that is not a key stays). A mapping with any cycle, including a SKU renamed to itself and a cycle that no item reaches, raises `ValueError`, also when there are no items. Every item is merged under its final SKU, so the merged item, its position and its conflicts use the final SKU, and no merged item keeps a SKU that is a key of the mapping. `read_renames(text)` reads a CSV text (any line ending) whose first non-blank row is the header `old_sku,new_sku` (cells trimmed) and returns `{old_sku: new_sku}` from the rows after it; rows whose cells are all blank are skipped and cells are trimmed. A missing or different header (also an empty text), a row without exactly 2 cells, a cell that is not a valid SKU (as `stockroom.models.check_sku` accepts), or an old SKU listed twice (even with the same new SKU) raises `stockroom.errors.ParseError`; a header alone gives `{}`, and a row renaming a SKU to itself is accepted by `read_renames` (the cycle is refused when merging). `merge_catalogues` takes an iterable of catalogues (each an iterable of `stockroom.models.Item`), `prefer`, which is `'first'` or `'last'` (anything else raises `ValueError`), and `renames`. All items are taken in one sequence, catalogue by catalogue and item by item; every appearance of a SKU after its first one (also inside the same catalogue) is merged into the item so far, one appearance at a time. The result has one item per SKU, in the order of each SKU's first appearance, with: the name of the last appearance for `prefer='last'` and of the first appearance for `prefer='first'`; the price in the same way, except that a price of 0 means "unknown" and never replaces a price, while a non-zero price always replaces a 0 (so the price is the last, or the first, non-zero price seen, or 0 when there is none); the tags of all appearances in order of first appearance, a tag being dropped when it equals an earlier one after `str.casefold()` (the first spelling stays, also within one item); and the largest reorder level seen. Whenever an appearance's name has a different `name_key` from the name the merged item has at that moment (the name in effect before this appearance), a `Conflict(sku, name_in_effect, new_name)` is recorded, in the order the appearances come. For a fixed `prefer`, merging is associative (merging the merge of the first catalogues with the rest gives the same items as merging all at once), and merging a result again, or twice, changes nothing. Finally add `python -m stockroom merge --out OUT [--prefer first|last] [--renames RENAMES] FILE [FILE ...]` (default `last`; at least one file, and a `--prefer` other than the two values is a usage error with exit code 2). It reads every file with `read_items` and the optional RENAMES file with `read_renames`, merges with those renames, writes `write_items` of the merged items to OUT (UTF-8), prints one warning line per conflict on stderr, `warning: SKU: name "BEFORE" differs from "AFTER"`, and prints `merged N items from K files` on stdout (`item` and `file` in the singular for 1). An unreadable catalogue, an unreadable RENAMES file (for example an old SKU listed twice) or a renames cycle exits with code 1, `stockroom: error: ...` on stderr, empty stdout and no OUT file. Existing behaviour otherwise stays.
acceptance: With the default `prefer='last'`, items keep the position of their first appearance and take the last name and the last non-zero price (a zero never replaces a price, a later price replaces a zero), the union of the tags without case-folded repeats in first-appearance order with the first spelling, and the largest reorder level; a duplicate inside one catalogue counts as a later appearance; empty inputs give `MergeResult((), ())`; iterators are accepted; the only conflict of the example is `Conflict('MUG-001', 'Blue Mug', 'Blue Mug XL')`

`prefer='first'` keeps the first name and the first non-zero price (a 0 is replaced by a later price, a later price never replaces a non-zero one), merges tags and reorder levels the same way, records `Conflict('PEN-100', 'Pen', 'Ink Pen')` and `Conflict('MUG-001', 'Blue Mug', 'Mug')` in that order and none for `BLUE  MUG`; the same input with `prefer='last'` gives the last names and prices; `First`, `both` and `''` raise `ValueError`

`name_key` gives `blue mug` for `Blue Mug`, for `BLUE`, two U+00A0, `mug` with spaces and a tab around it, and for a full-width `Ｂ`; `Straße` equals `STRASSE`, `e` + combining acute equals `é`, `ﬁne` gives `fine`, and for 1,000 seeded random names it is NFKC, whitespace joining and casefold; a conflict compares with the name in effect at that moment (`blue  mug` then `Red Mug`, and later `Ｒed Mug` then `Blue Mug` with `prefer='last'`; three conflicts against `Blue Mug` with `prefer='first'`), and spellings with the same key never conflict

For 1,500 seeded random triples of catalogues (five SKUs, names and tags that differ only in case, U+00A0 or `ß`/`SS`, zero and non-zero prices, both `prefer` values, and in half of the cases a seeded acyclic renames mapping, also into SKUs that otherwise never appear), the items and conflicts equal an independent computation of the stated rules, merging is associative both ways, merging the result again gives the same items and no conflicts, merging it with itself gives the same items, SKUs are unique and no merged SKU is a key of the renames mapping
